t: #2534 Time Taken to Cross the Door
o: We simulate seconds one at a time. At each second, everyone who has arrived but not yet crossed waits in one of two lines (enterers and exiters). The door's state last second decides priority: unused or last-exit favors exiters, last-enter favors enterers; ties break by index, which FIFO queues give us for free. In example 1, person 0 enters at t=0, so at t=1 and t=2 enterers keep priority over waiting exiter 1; once no enterers remain, person 1 exits at t=3. With n up to 1e5 and arrival times bounded by n, a simple simulation advancing second-by-second is linear in total time.
k: Two FIFO queues indexed by direction preserve the smallest-index-first tie-break automatically.
The door's previous-second usage is the only state needed besides the queues; an idle second resets it.
Total simulated time is O(max arrival + n), which is O(n) here.

a.i: Keep two deques of waiting people (state 0 and state 1) plus a pointer into the arrival-sorted array. Each second, admit everyone who arrived, pick who crosses based on `last` (the direction used last second, or none), and record their answer. If nobody crosses, reset `last` to none.
s: Initialize two empty deques, pointer i=0, clock t=0, last=-1.
Each second, push every person with arrival[p] <= t into their deque.
Pick an exiter if exiters exist and last != 0; otherwise an enterer if any; otherwise an exiter if any; record answer and set last accordingly.
If nobody was waiting, advance t without changing last except resetting it to -1 (door unused).
a.t: O(T) where T = max(arrival) + n <= 2n, since each second does O(1) work besides amortized queue pushes
a.sp: O(n) for the queues and answer

w: Simulate directly; the sorted arrivals make admission trivial. Pitfalls: forgetting that an idle second resets the door state (example 2 relies on exit-priority at t=0), and forgetting that a lone enterer crosses even after exits dominated previously. A follow-up might ask for the version where arrival is unsorted — sort indices by arrival first.
